reason: The capillary picture shows an empty inner face where the endothelial cells fit, so this looks like a clear first step toward the tissue route.
expectation: The lining should fit inside the support sleeves to form capillaries.

alternatives.reason: The lining might also fit inside the arterial wall, but the capillary picture shows the fit more explicitly.

effect: The lining and sleeves formed a capillary bed, whose thin walls allow exchange with fluid around cells.
reaction: The explicit fit made this a satisfying first piece.
reason: An artery also needs an inner lining, so I expect the endothelial sheet to fit inside the thick arterial wall.
expectation: This should make an artery with a lined inner surface.

effect: The lining also fits the arterial wall, forming vessels whose elastic walls stretch and recoil.
reaction: The pulse and rest views make the thick wall's role clearer.
reason: The venous wall should also need an inner lining before it can join the route.
expectation: This should form lined venous vessels.

effect: The endothelial lining formed thin-walled veins with the venous wall.
reaction: That matches the artery construction, though the vein wall looks different.
reason: The valve folds are pictured inside a vein, so they should fit the newly made veins.
expectation: The folds should form valves inside the veins.

effect: The valves complete a venous return model: muscle compression pushes blood toward the heart, while the valves resist backward flow.
reaction: The picture makes the valves' purpose clear.
reason: The goal calls for connecting arteries, capillaries and veins; arteries leading into the capillary bed seem like the next part of that route.
expectation: The arteries and capillaries should connect, leaving the veins to complete the return route.

effect: The arteries now branch into a capillary bed beside tissue cells; the return route still needs connecting.
reaction: The branching picture makes the distribution route clearer.
reason: The goal calls for veins to complete the route through tissues, and venous return is the remaining return-side piece.
expectation: The capillary bed should connect to the veins, completing a route out to tissues and back.

effect: Connecting venous return completed the systemic vessel network: arteries lead to capillaries, which join veins carrying blood back toward the heart.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate pieces form a complete route.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the venous valves was most worthwhile because the picture showed how muscle compression and valves help blood move toward the heart.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the lined arteries and veins felt somewhat repetitive, although their different wall shapes helped distinguish them.

surprise.text: I was surprised that contracting limb muscles help push blood through veins, with valves resisting backward flow.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goal made the fittings and route understandable.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: putting the vessel pieces together was satisfying, and I would be curious to see how the route connects with the rest of the body.
